title: Tamper-Evident Residence Ledger and Evidence Packager
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: Customers operating under SOC 2 and ISO 27001 frequently need bundled, tamper-evident evidence showing where data was processed, retention lifecycle events, and proofs that retention policies were applied. Current evidence exports are manual, missing chain-of-custody metadata, and do not preserve cryptographic markers across packaging operations.

Goal: Build an automated evidence packaging service that assembles time-series records, region tags, retention events, and access logs into a signed, tamper-evident bundle (the "Residence Ledger") suitable for auditors and internal compliance reviewers. The service should support configurable retention windows, reversible redaction metadata, and integration points for Dedicated/Private deployment environments.

Scope:
- Collectors: ingest SDK and runtime telemetry (service request headers, region, model variant, storage location), retention lifecycle events (delete, archive, hold), and proof artifacts (KMS-signed seals, file checksums).
- Packaging: produce a compressed bundle with an index, event timeline, chain-of-custody entries, and a cryptographic manifest signed by customer-managed KMS or Redwood service key.
- Residency assertions: label every event with region and jurisdiction and include an assertion layer that maps controls (SOC 2 CC6.x, ISO A.8.x) to evidence items.
- Replayability: support deterministic replays of the evidence timeline for auditor-led walkthroughs and export formats (PDF summary + NDJSON event stream).
- Ops: retention-aware purge rules, time-based snapshots, and automated notarization when retention thresholds are reached.

Out of scope for initial iteration: UI in Console (backend APIs only), advanced redaction policies requiring ML-based PII detection, and on-prem agent for air-gapped-only initial release (follow-up work).
acceptance_criteria: API endpoint returns a signed evidence bundle for a given customer and time window
Bundle contains an index file mapping events to control assertions (SOC 2 / ISO identifiers)
Signed manifest verifies correctly against configured KMS key (customer-managed or Redwood fallback)
Bundles include region and jurisdiction tags on every event and preserve original timestamps and sequence
Retention lifecycle events (delete/archive/hold) are represented and reversible-to-audit (redaction metadata not actual deleted content unless opt-in)
Automated nightly snapshot job shows generation metrics and failure alerts in the observability dashboard
Security review completed and threat-model mitigations documented
End-to-end integration test with ENG-76133 collector shows successful ingestion -> packaging -> signature verification
implementation_notes: Collectors will expose a standardized event envelope: {timestamp, source, region, event_type, payload_ref, checksum, control_map_ids}
Use an append-only event log for the evidence pipeline to ensure immutability semantics; consider Kafka/CloudPubSub with signed offsets
Packaging service will produce two artifacts: human-friendly summary (PDF) and machine-friendly NDJSON timeline; both included in tar.gz with manifest.sig
KMS integration: support AWS KMS and customer HSM via PKCS#11; fallback to Redwood signing key only when customer key not configured
Retention enforcement must not delete evidence bundles before configured retention windows expire; mark bundles as 'archived' and trigger notarization before purging
For private/VPC customers, ensure packaging runs inside customer boundary or that only signed manifests leave the VPC; coordinate with Private infra team on data egress controls
qa_notes: Create test fixtures simulating cross-region traffic and retention events across a 90-day window
Verify signature validation fails if bundle is tampered with (altered file, changed index, or timestamp modification)
Load test packaging pipeline with realistic event rates from Dedicated pools to validate SLA and queueing behavior
Run compliance scenario tests mapping evidence items to SOC 2 and ISO controls and document edge cases where mapping is ambiguous
comments: 2025-11-15 Aisha Khan: Initial writeup and scope; flagged need for customer KMS support early to satisfy enterprise customers.
2025-11-17 Luca Marino: Suggested dividing packaging into 'snapshot generation' and separate 'notarization' step to reduce latency for on-demand exports.
2025-11-18 Security Review (Ram Iyer): Require threat model review before integration with customer-managed keys; noted side-channel risk if signing happens in shared runtime.

2025-11-19 Eng tech note (Priya Singh): Prototype demonstrates signed manifest size ~4KB per bundle; recommended storing manifests in evidence index service and bundles in object storage with immutable flags.
2025-11-20 PM review (Aisha): Added acceptance criteria for replayability and integration test with ENG-76133. Next: schedule design review with infra and private deployment leads.
